function.mechanism: Anthocyanins are chromophoric flavonoid pigments that absorb visible light and impart red-purple-blue color in aqueous food systems.

adi.basis: EFSA ANS Panel (2013) temporarily accepted the previous ADI while noting specification/compositional data gaps for E163.

efsa.key_finding: No toxicological concern was identified for anthocyanins extracted from edible fruits and vegetables at reported uses, but the additive definition/specification was considered insufficiently characterized.

adi.basis: JECFA summary entry lists ADI as 0-2.5 mg/kg bw (16th meeting).

concerns.summary: EFSA exposure modeling indicated that high-level child consumers could exceed the temporary ADI in refined scenarios.
High-dose pro-oxidant and DNA-damage signals have been discussed in in vitro literature, but recent in vivo genotoxicity data for anthocyanin-rich extracts were negative.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2013: no toxicological concern for anthocyanins from edible fruits/vegetables at reported use levels.
2025 repeated-dose/genotoxicity package in rats reported no treatment-related adverse effects up to 5% dietary concentration.
2024 randomized trial reported no serious adverse events with blackcurrant anthocyanin supplementation.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined high-percentile exposure estimates reached up to 4.2 mg/kg bw/day, above the temporary ADI of 2.5 mg/kg bw/day in some child scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: E163 remains regulated/approved with generally low observed toxicity at typical uses, but EFSA identified specification uncertainty and potential ADI exceedance for high-consuming children, which supports an approved-with-caveats classification.
key_factors: EFSA 2013 no-toxicological-concern conclusion with temporary ADI retention
Exposure exceedance potential in high-percentile child consumers
Recent animal and human studies do not show strong serious-harm signals
